mathematics.scope: All word-Koszul Qn_dom objects have full indexed Ore for every n; the original nonKoszul problem remains open for n>=4. Every Q4dom has D3 and 3|N,3|L. Every D3 object with 3|L has at least two whole saturated r5 classes, with the proved pointwise r4 constraints. For arbitrary n with D3 and all r5=1, detP=detPB det(I-uvS^2) det(I-uv^2S^3), without 3|L, Koszul, noetherian, H or B-AS assumptions. The first unresolved n4 word is N9/L12; neither the determinant factorization nor the local bounds settle its existence or exclude it. Nozz implies full r5 at every period, and a period not divisible by six gives full ordinary skew Ore. No nonKoszul target example has been constructed or identified in the primary sources checked; residual possibilities are hypothetical.

mathematics.primary_source_details: research/BASELINE.md records bibliographic identifiers, exact locations, verified scope and unresolved source questions.

primary_texts_compared: Van den Bergh: Lemma 3.4, Definition 4.1.1, Theorem 4.2.2
Liu-Wang-Wu: Ore-extension theorem and connected graded scope
Iyudu-Shkarin: Theorem 1.11, Remark 1.15 and section 12.1, including the classification-free proof question in the ordinary case.
Presotto: Proposition 2.11 on right fraction categories of Z-domains with uniform rows.
Cassidy-Shelton: Theorems 1.5 and 3.6 on central extensions and finite-complexity PBW criteria.
Ardizzoni-Saracco-Stefan: Theorems 3.14 and 5.5, including general base rings and projectivity/homology hypotheses.
Issa-Lalin: published Theorems 1.1 and 1.2; the s=1 specialization of Theorem 1.2 used in the manuscript.
Ait Mohamed-El-Baz, arXiv:2611.15830v1: Theorem A and section 3. Comparison only; noetherian connected graded base and a pre-existing genuine Ore extension.
current_literature_review.limits: No exhaustive novelty determination. No publication version of ISclass was identified; its verified arXiv v1 metadata is retained. The 2026 Ore-descent preprint is a comparison in BASELINE, not a proof dependency.

retained_mixed_rank_proof.arithmetic: Integer Bareiss elimination with pivoting and exact-division checks; no floating point, random sampling or omitted cyclic representatives.
retained_mixed_rank_proof.scope: The canonical 890-array certificate and its source are unchanged. No fresh rerun or new independent implementation was executed in this revision.

weighted_baseline.scope: Hilbert/Euler, PBW and twisting baseline identities; retained certificate comparison.

skew_ore.scope: Four rewriting overlaps and the four displayed parameter components of dimensions 6,5,5,4; does not classify all moduli.

n4_pure_euler_formal_certificate.arithmetic: Python standard-library exact integers; no floating point or parameter sampling
n4_pure_euler_formal_certificate.fixed_data: s5,N7,L10,q=1; all input arrays are inside the script and in the note
n4_pure_euler_formal_certificate.all_degree_reduction: Cofactors have degree at most 45; (1-u^40)^3/det P has degree 70, so the numerator degree is at most 115. The first 120 coefficients determine the quadratic formula on every residue class.
n4_pure_euler_formal_certificate.scope: Pure formal Euler data only; no algebra or AS realization is asserted.

n4_parent_mixed_certificate.scope: Excludes one displayed mixed extension of the formal pure model; does not exclude all possible extensions.

exact_computation.proof_role: The retained 890-array certificate is a premise of the general n2 mixed-rank proof. Execution and source-preserving retention are recorded separately.
